instruction.text: The Earth is made up of different layers. Select the outermost layer.
instruction.sound: The Earth is made up of different layers. Select the outermohst layer.

feedback.end: The outermost layer is called the crust. The Earth’s crust is broken up into huge pieces called tectonic plates.
Tectonic plates are pieces of solid rock that are slowly, but constantly, moving. As they move, they can create mountains, volcanoes and even earthquakes.

atoms.b: Tectonic plates can move in different ways: they can ((++slide waddle)) alongside each other, ((++move sprint)) away from each other or move towards ((++each_other the_sea)), which is called converging.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: There are three main types of mountains that form when tectonic plates move. Fold mountains form when tectonic plates converge and push the ground upwards, lifting it to create a mountain.

Fault-block mountains form when tectonic plates move away from each other and break the Earth’s crust along weak lines called fault lines. When this happens, some blocks of land rise and others collapse.

Dome mountains are formed when the layer of molten rock underneath the Earth’s crust pushes its way upwards without breaking the surface. This forces the crust to bulge upwards before cooling and hardening into a mountain.
